name: Jehoshaphat
overview: Jehoshaphat was a male figure who served as one of King Solomon's twelve deputies, specifically overseeing the tribe of Issachar. His role as a deputy placed him in a position of leadership and responsibility during Solomon's reign. There are no additional notes or tribal affiliations provided beyond this unique attribute.
namesAndTitles: The name Jehoshaphat means 'YHWH has judged,' reflecting a theologically significant meaning rooted in the Hebrew understanding of God's judgment. This name appears in 1 Kings 4:17 and identifies him distinctly among Solomon's deputies.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Jehoshaphat was the father of Paruah, as explicitly stated in 1 Kings 4:17. No other family relationships are documented for him beyond this.
scriptureSignificance: Jehoshaphat's importance lies in his administrative role under King Solomon, contributing to the governance of Israel by managing the territory of Issachar. His position as one of the twelve deputies highlights the organized leadership structure during Solomon's reign. While he shares a name with the well-known king of Judah, this Jehoshaphat is distinct and serves as an example of faithful service in a governmental capacity within God's providential plan for Israel.

keyEvents.event: Allied with Ahab against Ramoth Gilead
